title: A Lightweight Interface to Connecticut Open Data APIs
text: package provides three primary functions: ct_list_datasets() retrieves live catalog available Connecticut Open Data datasets, including human-readable keys, Socrata UIDs, names, available metadata. ct_pull_dataset() downloads cataloged datasets using either human-readable key Socrata UID, support filtering, ordering, date ranges, optional column-name cleaning, optional type coercion. ct_any_dataset() downloads data directly valid Socrata JSON endpoint without requiring dataset appear package catalog. Datasets retrieved ct_pull_dataset() support arguments including: limit filters date date_field order clean_names coerce_types functions return tibble outputs. Advanced users may also provide raw SoQL conditions argument. SoQL, Socrata Query Language, query syntax used Socrata-powered Open Data portals. Additional information available Socrata developer documentation.

title: Pull any Connecticut Open Data dataset from a `Socrata` JSON endpoint — ct_any_dataset
code: # Examples that hit the live Connecticut Open Data API are guarded so CRAN # checks do not fail when the network is unavailable or slow. if (interactive() && curl::has_internet()) {   # Build a JSON endpoint from a `Socrata` UID   uid <- "ffju-s5c5"   endpoint <- paste0("https://data.ct.gov/resource/", uid, ".json")    out <- try(ct_any_dataset(endpoint, limit = 3), silent = TRUE)   if (!inherits(out, "try-error")) {     head(out)   } }

Supplying `uid` directly stable avoids ambiguity, keys provided readability classroom-friendly workflows. title: Pull a Connecticut Open Data dataset — ct_pull_dataset
code: if (interactive() && curl::has_internet()) {   # Pull by human-readable key   ct_pull_dataset("spill_incidents_from_july_1_2022_to_recent_for_download", limit = 3)    # Pull by `Socrata` UID   ct_pull_dataset("ffju-s5c5", limit = 3)    # Filter to one value   ct_pull_dataset(     "ffju-s5c5",     limit = 3,     filters = list(incident_type = "Petroleum Incident")   )    # Filter to multiple values   ct_pull_dataset(     "ffju-s5c5",     limit = 10,     filters = list(incident_type = c("Biomedical Incident", "Dielectric Fluid Incident"))   )    # Date filtering   ct_pull_dataset(     "ffju-s5c5",     from = "2023-01-01",     to = "2024-01-01",     date_field = "reported_date",     limit = 100   )    # Advanced filtering with raw SoQL   ct_pull_dataset(     "ffju-s5c5",     where = "incident_type = 'Petroleum Incident' AND township = 'New Haven'",     order = "reported_date DESC",     limit = 100   ) }
